subject: Cross-region Dedicated: throughput SLAs, DR topology, and packaging proposal
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura@brightscale.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity for BrightScale: multi-region sizing inquiry

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

We're starting procurement planning for a dedicated inference deployment and wanted to understand Redwood's options for multi-region Dedicated (separate GPU pools per region) vs an active-replicated topology. High level:
- Regions: primary us-east-1 (60% traffic), us-west-2 (30%), eu-west-1 (10%)
- Expected steady-state: ~4500 gen-tokens/sec (combined) with 2x short spikes for marketing events
- Models: a mix of 22B quantized variants and a heavier 70B for 15% of requests
- Need: throughput guarantees (SLA/RPS), options for replication/DR, and pricing bands for 12/24/36 month commits

Questions:
1) How do you price separate per-region pools vs active-active replication? Any replication multipliers?
2) Can we get an SLA for per-region 95th percentile latency and an overlay for failover time (RTO)?
3) What are your recommended commit sizes for our footprint and what discount tiers exist?

Procurement timeline: aiming to finalize vendor selection in the next 4–6 weeks. Please include approximate lead times for Dedicated onboarding + any verification checks (SOC2, network peering).

Thanks,
Laura
VP Product Ops
BrightScale Inc
(attachment: BrightScale_Machinery_Requirements.xlsx [application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet])

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@brightscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for BrightScale: multi-region sizing inquiry

Laura — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. Quick notes and follow-ups below.

Short answers up front:
- Pricing: separate per-region pools are priced per-region (you pay committed GPU-hours per pool). Active-active replication typically adds ~1.8–2.0x compute cost versus a single primary depending on model mix and whether KV/state replication is required.
- SLA/RTO: we can commit per-region latency SLOs and a failover RTO (tested during DR drills). SLA credits are scoped by region and route; will include SLOs in the proposal.
- Commit sizing: with your numbers my quick read suggests a committed baseline of 40–50 A100-equivalent units across regions (split), with burst/overflow options and a suggested safety buffer for the 70B usage.

Two follow-up asks:
1) Can you confirm the steady QPS or tokens/sec per region (sheet helps) and expected concurrency (peak simultaneous requests)?
2) Are you aiming for active-active (traffic actively balanced) or active-passive (standby in another region)? Active-active reduces RTO but increases committed compute cost.

I'll loop in Marissa (pricing lead) and Vivek (DR/architecture) — we can put together a short proposal with two packaging options: (A) Separate pools with cross-region failover (active-passive), (B) Active-active replicated pools with geo-routing. I'll aim to send a proposal by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura@brightscale.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for BrightScale: multi-region sizing inquiry

Aditya / team — thanks, answers below inline and I've added a couple clarifications in the sheet.

On sizing: steady-state tokens/sec per region ~ 2700 us-east, 1350 us-west, 450 eu-west. Peak concurrency: typically 4–5x sustained for short windows (5–10 minutes) during campaigns.

On replication topology: preference leaning toward active-passive to keep committed costs predictable, but open to active-active if the latency hit during failover is unacceptable.

Procurement: budget range is ~$1.2–1.8M ARR for infrastructure, but flexible if the pricing/SLAs warrant it. Looking for total landed cost including replication, routing egress, and any DR storage fees.

Timing: procurement and legal will require a 30–45 day review; SOC2 and network peering are mandatory — please call out lead times.

Thanks — looping procurement for visibility.

Laura
VP Product Ops
BrightScale Inc
(Bcc: Procurement <procurement@brightscale.com>)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@brightscale.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for BrightScale: multi-region sizing inquiry

Hey Laura — appreciate the details. Attached is a concise pricing + topology proposal (BrightScale_Pricing_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a diagram (multi-region-topology-diagram.png). High level summary here so procurement can triage quickly.

Option 1 — Separated pools (active-passive failover)
- Topology: Dedicated pool per region; standby capacity in failover region kept at 30% of primary by default (warm standby)
- Compute multiplier: ~1.0x committed compute (you pay per-region committed units; standby charged at reduced warm rate until failover)
- Pros: lowest committed compute cost, simpler egress accounting
- Cons: RTO dependent on warm-up and cache rehydration (~3–10 minutes depending on model size)

Option 2 — Active-active replicated pools
- Topology: Full active pools in us-east and us-west; replication keeps KV caches partially warm; eu as smaller active pool
- Compute multiplier: ~1.8–2.0x (replicated state and steady compute in both regions)
- Pros: near-immediate failover, consistent latency during events
- Cons: higher ARR, cross-region egress and replication bandwidth costs

Pricing bands (indicative) — 12 / 24 / 36 month commits (all $ in USD, ARR basis)
- 12 mo: base pricing (no deep commit) — estimated $1.45M ARR for Option 1 profile above
- 24 mo: ~8% discount off 12-mo band — estimated $1.33M ARR
- 36 mo: ~13% discount off 12-mo band — estimated $1.26M ARR
- Active-active uplift: multiply band by 1.9x for compute + ~add 3–5% for bandwidth/replication services

SLA and credits
- We can commit to 95th percentile p95 latency SLOs per-region per-route. For multi-region failover RTO we propose an SLO of 5 minutes for automated failover (active-active) or 10 minutes for warm-standby (active-passive), with financial credits tied to missing RTO targets. We'll draft specific credit language for procurement.

Operational notes
- Onboarding lead time: 3–6 weeks after contract signature (SOC2 evidence and network peering must be validated in parallel; longer if private peering requested)
- Security: we will provide SOC2 Type II artifacts and a platform security workbook; we support customer KMS integration for keys in Private deployments
- Routing: recommend using our smart routing policy with regional preference + overflow to nearest compatible region; cross-region egress billed per cloud egress norms (we will include estimates per region)

Next steps
1) I'll upload the formal proposal PDF and topology diagram to the HubSpot deal and share a DocuSign for a mutual action plan.
2) If legal needs, we'll supply draft SOW language and an SLA appendix.
3) Aditya / Vivek: can you confirm the recommended committed unit split (A100 equivalents) across regions with the 70B penalty factored in?

Attaching: BrightScale_Pricing_Proposal_v1.pdf, multi-region-topology-diagram.png

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Deals
Redwood Inference
(attachment: BrightScale_Pricing_Proposal_v1.pdf [application/pdf])
